newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Weifu sees slim rise in H1 net.
newsitem.headline: China's Weifu sees slim rise in H1 net.

text.p: Chinese automobile parts maker Weifu Fuel Injection Co Ltd expects net profits for the first half of this year to be slightly above the 33.20 million yuan ($4.0 million) in the 1996 period, a company official said on Tuesday.
The rise would reflect cost reductions that helped offset the impact of sluggish domestic auto sales, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The official declined to give an estimate of interim profits though the company had previously estimated a five percent rise in earnings.
Weifu, based in Wuxi city in east China's Jiangsu province, slashed its payrolls by about 10 percent to some 2,200 during the first six months of this year, the official said.
China's automobile sales remained depressed in the first half, capping Weifu's earnings, he said.
The company's accounts receivable ballooned in the period, the official added but declined to give figures.
Weifu's accounts receivable stood at 169 million yuan at end-1996, compared with 143 million yuan at the end of 1995.
The firm posted net profits of 67.39 million yuan for 1996 against 65.63 million for the previous year based on Chinese accounting standards.
Under international standards, Weifu booked 66.73 million yuan in net profits for last year against 62.98 million yuan for 1995.
